Emily: heads up — after the kernel-selector change rolled yesterday we see steady KV slot residency growth under longctx workloads on Dedicated :eyes:
Raf: can you paste the metric?
Emily: kv.slot_residency_p50=1200ms, p90=9.2s, slots_used jumped from 48% -> 95% over 2h. grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/kv-longctx
Sonya: noticed a small quality drift on the quantized BF16->INT8 path too. eval run on conv-turns shows ~0.8% top-token shift, not huge but correlated in time.
Emily: payload: long dialogs (avg seq 6k tokens) => many KV pages reloaded. suspect a combination of: the new kernel picks aggressive single-threaded attention kernels + our old dormancy heuristic not lowering residency for INT8 pages.
Raf: repro steps I used: run tools/synth_longctx.py --model redwood-7b-int8 --seq 6k --qps 3 for 45m. it reproduces memory climb. attaching small trace:
Raf: ```
# rdkvctl dump
model: redwood-7b-int8
slots_total: 524288
slots_in_use: 498732
avg_residency_ms: 7321
page_faults_last_5m: 1240
compaction_runs: 0
```
KV-bot: [alert] kv-residency-growth redwood-7b-int8 at 2024-11-08T16:34Z — auto-tagged regression (rule: residency>5s p90)
Mike: compaction_runs: 0 stands out. compactor might be gated by a flag that the new kernel path doesn't set. happy to add a guard so compaction runs from the eviction path for quantized pages.
Sonya: accuracy numbers from eval harness (same period): PPL +1.2, exact-match -0.6%, token-shift ~0.8%. not catastrophic but could escalate if residency keeps rising.
Raf: quick heap profile (abridged):
Raf: ```
# go pprof output (kv heap)
1.2GB  45.0%  kv.page_cache
0.6GB  22.5%  kv.slot_meta
0.4GB  15.0%  runtime.heap
```
Emily: hypothesis: INT8 path reduces memory per slot but increases fragmentation and prevents the eviction path from compacting because slot-coalesce expects fp-aligned layouts. result: many small fragments pinned, so reuse drops.
Mike: mitigation options:
- very short term: background compaction cron every 5m (cheap)
- short term: force compaction on eviction for pages older than X ms if page_frag_ratio>Y
- medium term: add per-model dormancy thresholds + sequence-length-aware policy
Jen: for rollout plan: create canary on Dedicated pool A (10% traffic) with compaction cron enabled + a metric dashboard: kv.slot_residency_p50/p90, kv.compaction_runs, kv.page_frag_ratio, model-output-drift (eval set). rollback if slot_residency p90 > 10s or eval drift > 1.5%.
Raf: I can prototype the eviction-path compaction patch. quick sketch: on eviction path, if page_frag_ratio>0.4 and model.quant==INT8 then trigger compaction_async(page_id). also log a sample of affected slots to /var/log/kv/compaction-samples.log
Sonya: also recommend adding a precision-checker in the CI eval harness: run small eval on canary every 30m to detect drift within minutes.
Emily: agree. I'll open two PRs: (1) eviction-triggered compaction + async worker; (2) per-model dormancy config + runtime override. I'll wire the canary and the eval checks.
Mike: thumbs for the plan. I'll add the cron as a stopgap on prod infra. :thumbsup:
KV-bot: [deploy-bot] scheduled cron kv-compactor-every-5m to pool-dedicated-A (ops ticket #INC-9921)
Jen: please add an entry in the change log and ping SRE for the canary window. also tag Product since there is an observable perf/quality tradeoff.
Emily: final note — let's capture a before/after snapshot (pprof + kv dump + eval) at t0 and t+1h. Raf, ping me when you have the patch so we can coordinate canary injection.
Raf: will do, prepping patch now.
Emily: thanks all — keeping this thread as the coordination point. :rocket:
